clue.text: A nameless visionary, smelling nice

indicators.note: nameless tells us to drop the abbreviation for name from the word that follows

parts.note: a visionary is an idealist or romantic

explanation.surface: An anonymous dreamer happens to give off a pleasant scent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visionary' reads as a noun in the surface, a seer, but here it means a dreamy idealist; 'nameless' drops the N for name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with a pleasant, spicy fragrance is described as having an agreeable smell, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Make contact with everyone after conclusion of affair

indicators.note: after places the following piece in front of the word for everyone
the conclusion of a word is its final letter, so only the end of affair is used

parts.note: each person, everyone taken one by one

explanation.surface: Getting in touch with everybody once a love affair has ended.
explanation.walkthrough: The R that ends 'affair' is put before EACH because 'after' says EACH follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach someone is to get through to them by phone or message, a synonym for making contact.

clue.text: Lose opportunity with young woman who accepts honour the wrong way

parts.note: miss is a title for a young unmarried woman

indicators.note: accepts means one word takes another inside it

parts.note: who can be replaced by that in a relative clause

indicators.note: the wrong way means the honour's letters are read backwards

parts.note: the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A girl who received an award but held it upside down missed her chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who' looks like a link word but supplies letters as 'that'. The OBE is an award given by the British monarch; 'the wrong way' turns it before 'accepts' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means failing to take a chance while it is available, like arriving after a ship has sailed.

clue.text: Time curtain's redrawn or withdrawn

indicators.note: redrawn suggests the letters are pulled into a different arrangement

parts.note: curtain's gives the letters of curtain; the possessive adds none

explanation.surface: A stage curtain is pulled back again, or perhaps pulled shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redrawn' rearranges T plus CURTAIN. The surface makes 'redrawn' and 'withdrawn' look like a pair of curtain movements.
explanation.definitionFit: A withdrawn person keeps to themselves and says little, which is what reserved and silent describes.

clue.text: Composer, poet and president

parts.note: Samuel Taylor Coleridge was an English Romantic poet
Zachary Taylor was the twelfth US president

explanation.surface: A list naming a musician, a writer and a head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Coleridge-Taylor was an English composer of the early twentieth century, best known for Hiawatha's Wedding Feast.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Coleridge-Taylor was a British composer, so the name is an example of the category.

clue.text: Opening comment of doctor interrupting walk

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of the word for walk

parts.note: gait is a way of walking
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A physician butts in on a stroll with an opening remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambit can be a remark made to open a conversation, as well as a chess opening.

clue.text: Idle talk over a wife's way of expressing amusement

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the first piece above what follows

parts.note: guff is nonsense or empty talk
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: After all the gossip, how does a married woman show she finds it funny?
explanation.definitionFit: A loud hearty laugh is one manner of showing that something amuses you.

clue.text: Kind of cap for Mafiosi

definitions.meaning: a soft frilled indoor cap once worn by women
a name for organised crime gangs

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an old-fashioned bonnet and a gang of organised criminals.

clue.text: Everything I brought up kid wound up

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means the words for everything and I are read upwards

parts.note: all means everything
to kid is to tease or rib

explanation.surface: Raising a child left someone thoroughly agitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns ALL plus I into ILLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wound up is being tense and nervous, which is feeling uncomfortable and anxious.

clue.text: Analyse speed of light: it takes years to get this far

definitions.text: it takes years to get this far

parts.note: to parse a sentence is to analyse its grammar
c is the physics symbol for the speed of light

explanation.surface: A physics student studies light speed and the vast distances it covers over years.
explanation.walkthrough: A parsec is about 3.26 light years, so light takes years to cross one.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronomical unit of distance is so large that even light needs over three years to travel it.

clue.text: This could preserve shattered belief held by officer

indicators.note: held by means the jumbled letters sit inside the officer's abbreviation

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

indicators.note: shattered means broken up, so the letters of belief are rearranged

explanation.surface: An officer clings to a broken faith.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole opening 'This could preserve': a lifebelt preserves life; 'shattered' scrambles the belief and 'held by' wraps the lieutenant round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A buoyant ring thrown to someone in the water keeps them alive, so it preserves life.

clue.text: Brief note from an impudent girl

definitions.meaning: a short written note or voucher
a dismissive word for a cheeky young woman

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a short memo or IOU and a pert, saucy young girl.

clue.text: Treat actor badly, producing statuette, perhaps

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are handled poorly and so disordered

explanation.surface: Mistreating a performer leads to an award figurine.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fired-clay figure is an example of the brownish-red earthenware, so the material stands for the object.

clue.text: Pleased cow went here

definitions.meaning: being delighted is described by an idiom about extreme happiness
in the nursery rhyme Hey Diddle Diddle the cow jumped above Earth's satellite

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for great delight comes from the rhyme where a cow leaps over the night sky's satellite.

clue.text: Shabby old magistrate, a revolutionary

parts.note: the Doge was the chief magistrate of old Venice and Genoa
red is a word for a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A former official, once a radical, is now looking worn.
explanation.definitionFit: Pages with folded-down corners look worn and tatty, so the word means shabby.

clue.text: Waver between various options, devel minute, oping local site

clue.text: Style on show in Iceland

indicators.note: on show in says the letters are visible inside the next word

explanation.surface: A fashion statement displayed in Iceland.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is flair and dash, a synonym for style.

clue.text: Spectator, a weekly publication

definitions.meaning: A British Sunday newspaper, published once a week

explanation.walkthrough: The Spectator is itself a British weekly magazine, which helps the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an onlooker and also names a weekly Sunday newspaper in Britain.

clue.text: Sound following English church round

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A noise heard after an English church bell is rung.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a reflected sound heard again, so it is a kind of sound.

clue.text: Sour note broadcaster has introduced

indicators.note: has introduced means the note is put inside the word for broadcaster

parts.note: an emitter sends out signals, as a broadcaster does
B is a musical note

explanation.surface: A radio station drops in a bitter message.
explanation.definitionFit: To sour someone is to make them resentful, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Deal cheerfully with problem getting Rupert out of bed

parts.note: Rupert Bear is a British cartoon character
being up means risen from bed

explanation.surface: Rousing a sleepy boy called Rupert is a challenge to face with good humour.
explanation.walkthrough: Rupert Bear is a long-running British children's comic-strip bear.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear up is to cope bravely and stay cheerful under difficulty, an idiom.

clue.text: With it, whether or not silver's involved

definitions.text: With it, whether or not silver's involved

indicators.note: involved means silver's symbol is wrapped inside the phrase

parts.note: all there means mentally alert, with it
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone is trendy whether or not they wear silver.
explanation.walkthrough: Without AG the phrase reads ALL THERE (alert); with AG inside it reads the answer (fashionable). Both mean 'with it', so 'whether or not' holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fashionable or in vogue is a sense of being with it, as is being alert.

clue.text: Inch of hem

definitions.meaning: to inch is to move slowly little by little
a hem is the border of a garment

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to creep forward gradually and a border or rim of cloth.

clue.text: Fancy points seen in practical cat

indicators.note: seen in means the compass points appear inside the cat's name

parts.note: Gus the Theatre Cat is in T. S. Eliot's Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats
E and S are compass points

explanation.surface: Points of interest spotted in a sensible cat.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something can mean to suppose or surmise it, a synonym for this verb.

clue.text: Boot out of castle

definitions.meaning: a type of laced ankle boot
... Castle is the royal family's Scottish home

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to a royal Scottish residence and also to a style of laced boot named after it.

clue.text: River's rising — get a waterproof

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the river's name reads upwards

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

explanation.surface: With the river climbing, grab a raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A mac, short for mackintosh, is a raincoat, a waterproof garment.

clue.text: No name given to wild flower

indicators.note: no name given to means the letter for name is dropped

parts.note: violent means wild or uncontrolled

explanation.surface: An unidentified wild bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No name given to' drops N from VIOLENT.
explanation.definitionFit: The violet is a small purple-flowered plant, an example of a flower.

clue.text: Policeman departs during summing-up

indicators.note: during means the abbreviation sits within the summary word

parts.note: a recap is a summing-up
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: An officer walks out while the judge gives the summary.
explanation.walkthrough: A redcap is British slang for a military policeman, from their red caps.
explanation.definitionFit: A redcap is a member of the Royal Military Police in Britain, so a kind of policeman.

clue.text: Scarcity of earners working, and beginning to save

indicators.note: working means the letters of earners are set to work in a new order
beginning to picks only the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Workers finding it hard to save money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges EARNERS to RARENES; 'beginning to' adds the S of save.
explanation.definitionFit: Rareness is the quality of being uncommon, the same as scarcity.
